Prebuilt **Linux and Windows x86-64** binaries of `k3`, the pure-C Kimi K3 inference
engine from [FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c),
built with the Tiny C Compiler (TCC) only.

**This release makes the TCC build's matrix kernels about 5x faster.** The output is
bit-identical to [v1.2.0](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/releases/tag/v1.2.0) and
every earlier build. Nothing else changes: the same features, the same downloads, and
the same system requirements. If you use v1.2.0, upgrade.

## What changed

The scalar matrix-vector kernels were rewritten in plain C to suit how TCC compiles.
TCC doesn't inline functions, doesn't keep values in registers between statements, and
turns every `fma()` into a call into the C library. The hot loops were paying for two
function calls per element.

- **Named accumulators.** Each of the 16 accumulators (8 for MXFP4) is its own
  variable instead of an array slot.
- **Plain multiply and add instead of `fma()`.** Every product in these kernels fits
  exactly in a double, so rounding it changes nothing and the result is the same bit for
  bit.
- **Activations widened once.** The input vector is converted to double once per call,
  not once per row.
- **bf16 lookup table.** bf16 weights are widened through a 65536-entry double table
  (512 KB, built on first use).
- **MXFP4 lookup table.** MXFP4 weights are decoded straight from the packed bytes
  through a byte-to-two-doubles table.

Every accumulator keeps the same position and every sum the same order, so the test
fixtures and the reference comparison still match exactly.

## Performance

Kernel benchmark (`tcc -run build.c bench`) on a 4-core Xeon at real Kimi K3
dimensions, 4 threads, three runs each. The v1.2.0 and v1.2.1 builds were measured back
to back:

| Kernel | v1.2.0 | v1.2.1 |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 matmul 12288 x 7168 | 200.9 / 164.4 / 170.9 ms | 43.8 / 33.1 / 31.2 ms |
| MXFP4 matmul 3072 x 3584 | 29.6 / 28.5 / 22.6 ms | 5.06 / 5.90 / 4.73 ms |

- **Against GCC:** the gap to the old GCC AVX2 build
  ([v1.1.0-win.1](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/releases/tag/v1.1.0-win.1)) is now
  roughly 3-4x on bf16 and 4-5x on MXFP4, down from about 14x. The GCC timings come from
  an earlier session on the same machine, and timings there vary by tens of percent
  between sessions, so treat that ratio as approximate.
- **Real inference:** a full model run gains less than the kernel figures wherever
  reading weights from disk dominates, as it does on the low-memory presets.

## Downloads

| File | Runs on |
|---|---|
| `k3-1.2.1-windows-x64.zip` | 64-bit Windows Vista or later, any x86-64 CPU |
| `k3-1.2.1-linux-x64.zip` | 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.38 or newer (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39), any x86-64 CPU |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums for both zips |

Each zip contains `k3` (`k3.exe` on Windows), `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `README.txt`.

- **No installer and no extra DLLs.**
  - `k3.exe` imports only `kernel32.dll` and `msvcrt.dll`.
  - The Linux `k3` needs only `libc.so.6` and `libm.so.6`.
- **Verify the download.**
  - PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\k3-1.2.1-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256`
  - Linux: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`
- **Quick check:** `k3 --version` should print `k3 1.2.1`.

Running inference needs the Kimi K3 checkpoint (about 1.56 TB), which you download
separately. See
[docs/QUICKSTART.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.1/docs/QUICKSTART.md).

## How it was built and verified

- **Build:** [`release.yml`](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.1/.github/workflows/release.yml)
  on GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` runners, with TCC 0.9.28rc (TinyCC
  commit `e23dabed`).
- **Full test suite** on each OS before packaging: `22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`,
  `VERDICT: ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY`, `ALL WEIGHTLESS TESTS PASSED`.
- **Same output as v1.2.0:**
  - the benchmark's output digests are unchanged;
  - the kernel tests pass at 1, 3 and 4 threads, including the bitwise check that the
    bf16 and fp32 kernels agree.
- **Not verified:** inference on real Kimi K3 weights with the TCC build, and tokenizer
  parity. Both need the checkpoint, which CI does not have.

Full history: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.1/CHANGELOG.md).
